info.title: Lodestar API
info.description: Every node is a new discovery. The JSON API under `/api/v1` (architecture §9): errors are always the `Error` envelope, and every path but the auth ones and this document needs the session cookie.

get.summary: Whether the instance is set up and the caller logged in.

Your classification rules, and how detection compares with your
corrections.

post.summary:
Your classification correction for one stored torrent; it's
classified again at once.

Adds a classification rule; the stored torrents it matches are
classified again. At most 1,000 rules: past that, 422
`too_many_class_rules`.

Removes a classification rule; the torrents it matched are classified
again without it.

get.description:
Each frame is `id: <epoch>-<seq>` (none on `resync`), `event: <name>`
and `data: <json>`, the payload of the `Event` variant of that name.
Send the last id back as `Last-Event-ID` (`EventSource` does) to
replay what was missed; when that can't be done exactly (a restart,
too long ago, or an id that isn't ours), a `resync` comes first. A
client that falls behind gets a `resync` and carries on from live. A
comment every 15 s keeps the connection open; `retry:` is 5 s.

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description:
Comma-separated topics, e.g. `torrents,crawler`; all of them when
absent. An unknown or empty one is a 400 with `field: "topics"`.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last `id:` received, to resume after it.

200.description: The stream: one `Event` per frame (`event:` names the variant, `data:` holds its payload).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: `no`, so a proxy doesn't buffer it.

429.description: Too many open streams, in all or for this session (`too_many_streams`).

503.description: Not served here, or shutting down (`events_unavailable`).

get.summary: The rule set, switches and lists.

post.summary:
Applies a change. A change that weakens filtering is refused with 428
(`confirm_required`, the assessment beside the error) until it's sent
again with the admin password, every time (§20.11).

get.summary: The core rules' hashed examples, run against the rules as they are.

post.summary:
What a change would do, without applying it or asking for the
password.
Starts a preview in the background; poll it by its id.

get.summary:
A preview job: progress while it runs, then the assessment (or the
error) once it's done.

post.summary: Cancels a preview job; it stops at its next step.

get.summary:
The review queue: quarantine (never with names) and the last 30 days'
decisions per rule.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Quarantine rows per page: 1–1000, 1000 by default.

post.summary:
How strict a candidate set of lists is (§2.9, §20.13): what it
would block and a warning matched to it. Nothing is stored or
connected.

Tries a draft rule and the current rules on example torrents. Nothing
is stored or logged.

get.summary:
Tombstones (dropped torrents) by hash and rule, never with names, in
pages; `adult=true` lists only adult holds.

parameters.name: adult
parameters.description:
Only adult holds: torrents held because you relabelled them adult,
which the 30-day purge left as tombstones.

200.description: Logged in; the session cookie is set.

post.summary: Clears the session cookie. The body is ignored but must be JSON.

get.summary:
Parses a query: the AST and its canonical text, or a `query_syntax`
error whose `start`/`end` span the UI highlights.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text; empty matches everything.

post.summary: Changes the password and ends every other session.

200.description: Changed; a new session cookie is set.

get.summary: Searches with query text. To search with an AST, POST it.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text; empty browses everything.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `relevance` (the default), or `discovered`, `size` or `files` with an optional `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending, the default).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: `offset + limit` may not pass 10,000. Not with `cursor`.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `next_cursor`; send the same `q`, `sort` and `hidden` with it. An expired one is a 410 `cursor_expired`, a tampered one a 400 `bad_cursor`.

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: `1` or `true`: count every match exactly, within a time budget.

post.summary: Searches with query text or a query AST.

get.summary:
Every settings section, with the fields and JSON schema its form is
generated from.
get.description:
Each property of a section's schema carries hints for the form (the
server checks everything regardless): `x-group` (the group's id; its
heading is the message `settings.group.<id>`), `x-order`, `x-advanced`,
`x-preview` (`POST /settings/preview` has estimates or warnings for
it) and, where they apply, `x-unit` (`seconds`, `mebibytes`,
`connections`), `x-widget` (`radio`, `slider`, `theme`, `shortcuts`,
`language`, `time-zone`), `x-auto` (the value that means "automatic"),
`x-keywords` (a message key of search synonyms), `x-danger`
(`disruptive`, `privacy`, `destructive`, `security`, §10.10.7),
`x-config` (the `config.toml` key), `x-env` (the `LODESTAR_*`
variable), `format` (`socket-addr`, `log-filter`) and `writeOnly`
(a secret, never sent back).

patch.summary:
Changes several sections at once (`{section: {field: value}}`), as a
screen showing fields from several sections saves them: every
section's patch is checked as `PATCH /settings/{section}` checks it,
then all are saved in one transaction. One refused field saves
nothing; the error names its `section` and `field`.

409.description: `read_only`, `set_by_environment`, or `stale_revision` with each stale section's `current` values.

get.summary:
The saved settings as a TOML file to keep or move to another install,
laid out by section (`[crawler]`), each key with its `config.toml`
key and environment variable in a comment. It holds only values saved
in the app: never a secret, a value an environment variable sets, or
filter, floor, pack or subscription state (§20 has its own export).
`preferences` is included only when asked.

post.summary:
Reads a file from `GET /settings/export` and reports what it would
change. Keys that aren't settings, read-only ones, secrets and ones an
environment variable sets are listed in `skipped` and left alone.
Unless `dry_run=true`, the changes are then saved as one batch with
`PATCH /settings`' checks: all or nothing.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Only report what the import would change (the diff); save nothing.

409.description: `stale_revision`: a section changed since the dry run's `revisions`.

422.description: `invalid_import` (not an export file), or a value `PATCH /settings` refuses (`invalid_setting`, `adult_confirmation_required`). Nothing is saved.

post.summary:
What `PATCH /settings` with the same body would do, without saving:
the same checks and refusals, then for each patched field whether it
applies now or after a restart, warnings, and estimates where the
section can make them (fetch sockets, the new address, memory).

Tests a download client with the values on screen, before they're
saved: logs in and asks its version. It goes through the integrations
SSRF guard (download clients may be on this machine or the LAN, never
on link-local, metadata or reserved addresses). Nothing is saved, and
the result never repeats the URL or a credential.

200.description: The test ran; `ok` says whether it passed.

422.description: `bad_body`: not a test this endpoint runs.

get.summary:
One section's effective values, where each comes from, which can't be
changed here or wait for a restart, and its revision.

patch.summary:
Changes some of a section's settings. Every field is checked first,
then all are saved together; live ones apply at once, and the rest
are listed in `restart_required`. A field an environment variable
sets is refused, naming the variable. With `if_revision`, a section
changed since is refused with its current values.

422.description: `invalid_setting`; `adult_confirmation_required`: turning on an adult setting without `"confirm_adult": true`. Nothing is saved.

post.summary:
Claims a fresh instance with the setup token from the logs and a new
password; logs in.

200.description: Set up; the session cookie is set.

get.summary: One torrent by any of its swarm hashes.

404.description: `torrent_not_found`, or `adult_hidden`: an Adult torrent while "Show adult content" is off.

get.summary: A page of a torrent's file list.

404.description: `torrent_not_found`, or `adult_hidden`: an Adult torrent while "Show adult content" is off.

AlertsEvent.description:
`event: alerts` (reserved: B9 publishes it): a saved search matched
new torrents. The matches themselves come from the API.

version.description: The rule set's version after the change.

Assessment.description: A change's assessment (§20.10, §20.11). Field order: see [`Preview`].

confirm.description:
The password is needed (every weakening change, and marking a list
as part of the locked floor).

floor_entries.description:
For a floor removal: the entries the warning counts, 40 hex digits
each. A removal settles at most 10,000 at a time, so a longer
pending list goes in batches. Send these back as `hashes` to
confirm the removal with the password.

oneOf.description: For a keyword override: the same entry as *Neutralize term*.

warning.description: The plain-language effect warning; null for a strengthening change.

oneOf.description: Matches everything (an empty query: browse).
A word, tokenized when compiled.
Inclusive bounds; null is open.
Inclusive bounds; null is open.
File extensions; matches any.
40 lowercase hex digits.
A keyword facet; matches any of the values.
Torrents with at least one file matching every clause of `of`.
A category's share of the files or bytes, inclusive percentages.

AstWhen.description:
One end of a date range: seconds before the search (`ago`), or a Unix
time (`at`).

setup_required.description:
No password yet: claim the instance with the setup token from the
logs.

oneOf.description: A pack (`malware`) or one pack rule (`MW-2`).

unless.description: An empty string removes the clause.

oneOf.description: Report torrents as child-abuse material (§20.5.2).

A quarantined torrent a rule caught wrongly (§20.12): an exception
for that torrent and that rule only, a hashed must-not-match
fixture for a core rule, and a release.

Releases a quarantined or dropped torrent: fetched and processed
normally next time it's seen.

Confirms a quarantined torrent as abuse material: into CS-1, sealed
name deleted.
Accepts or discards a version the sanity gates held back.

Settles floor entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped
(owner's decision §2.7). They stay blocked until this: `remove`
takes them out of the floor, which weakens it; otherwise they stay
in it as ordinary CS-1b entries. `source` is a pending source's key
(`file:<path>`, `list:<id>`).

A removal confirmed with the password must name its entries: send
back the assessment's [`Assessment::floor_entries`], so the
password confirms what the warning listed. Keeping may leave
`hashes` out, which keeps what the assessment counted.

Change.description: One change to filtering (§20.7), tagged by `op`.

ChangeBody.description:
`POST /filters/preview`, `/filters/preview/jobs` and `/filters/apply`.
`Debug` shows whether a password was sent, never the password.

password.description:
The admin password, for a change that weakens filtering (§20.11);
ignored by previews.

queued.description:
Stored torrents queued to be classified again; null without a
search index (only torrents arriving later are affected).

truncated.description:
More stored torrents matched than are queued at once (1,000,000):
the rest are classified again when next re-enriched.

query.description: Can't test `type:` or `adult:`: the rule decides them.

Classes.description:
`GET /classify`: your classification rules, and how detection
compares with your per-torrent corrections (§20.9).

CompositionShare.description: One colour group's share of a torrent (`docs/metrics.md` §4, §7.1).

bytes.description: Bytes in the group, padding excluded.

files.description: Files in the group, padding excluded.

pct_bytes.description:
Whole percent of the non-padding bytes: any non-zero share is at
least 1, and only a complete one is 100.

pct_files.description: The same, of the non-padding files.

floor.description: Part of the locked floor: can't be switched off.

CorrectBody.description:
`POST /classify/correct`: your correction to one stored torrent,
replacing any earlier one. `adult: null` and `not_junk: false` clear it.

held_by.description:
When relabelling it adult made filtering hold it back (§20.9): the
rule that did. It's then dropped or quarantined, no longer stored.

CrawlerEvent.description:
`event: crawler`: the same counters as the status page and
`/metrics`, sent every 5 s while anyone subscribes.

dht_nodes.description:
Nodes in the DHT routing table; null when the DHT is off or
hasn't reported yet.

harvested.description: Hashes received from sources since start.

shadow.description: Decided in shadow mode: recorded, not acted on.

checked.description: Corrections that say adult or not.

disagree.description: Of those, ones detection gets wrong.

DownloadClientDraft.description: A download client's settings as the form has them, unsaved.

password.description:
The password (qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission and rTorrent with
authentication) or the RPC secret (Aria2).

url.description: The client's address, as the form has it.

username.description:
The user name (qBittorrent; Transmission and rTorrent with
authentication).

DownloadClientKind.description: A download client a connection test can reach.

code.description: A stable snake_case identifier to branch on.

end.description:
The end of the fault's byte span within `field` (query syntax
errors).

field.description: The request parameter or body field at fault (`sort`, `ast.field`).

start.description: The start of the fault's byte span within `field`.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
`{ "error": { … } }`, plus the rare top-level key a client needs to
recover.

assessment.description:
On a 428 from `POST /filters/apply`: the warning to show before
asking for the password.

setup_required.description: On a 401: whether the instance still needs its first-run setup.

Event.description:
One frame of the stream: `event:` names the variant and `data:` holds
its payload. Every event but `resync` has an `id:` of the form
`<epoch>-<seq>` to send back as `Last-Event-ID`.

FieldPreview.description: One patched field, as it would be saved.

restart_required.description: It would apply at the next restart; otherwise at once.

value.description: The value it would have (null for a secret).

FilesPage.description: `GET /torrents/{hash}/files`: a page of the file list.

failing.description: Examples the rule now gets wrong.

Fixtures.description:
`GET /filters/fixtures`: the core rules' hashed examples, run against
the rules as they are (§20.8).

from_source.description:
Where the value now comes from: to undo, send it back, or `null`
when this isn't `db`.

restart_required.description: It applies at the next restart.

ImportReport.description: `POST /settings/import`: the diff, and whether it was applied.

applied.description: Saved (false on a dry run, or when nothing changes).

revisions.description:
Every section's revision after the import: pass them back with
the real import to refuse it if anything changed after a dry run.

unchanged.description: Settings in the file that already have its value.

ImportSkip.description: A key in the file that an import leaves alone.

env.description: The variable that sets it, for `set_by_environment`; null otherwise.

key.description: `section.field`, or the key as the file has it.

InsightsEvent.description:
`event: insights` (reserved: B11a publishes it every 30 s): the stage
strip's headline numbers (`docs/metrics.md` §6.1, §7.5).

JobStatus.description:
`GET /filters/preview/jobs/{id}`: progress while it runs, then the
assessment or the error.

error.description: Once `failed`: the error the preview would have returned.

MatchInput.description:
What an override, exception or allow entry matches, as sent: exactly
one of the four.

OkResponse.description: The body of a write that has nothing else to say.

scope.description: Applies only to what this query matches; null = everything.

Overview.description:
`GET /filters`: the rule set, switches and lists, as the Filters &
Safety screens show them.

pending_floor_removals.description:
Entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped, still blocked
until you settle them (§2.7).

ParseResponse.description: `GET /parse`: the AST and the canonical text it prints as.

PasswordRequest.description:
`POST /password`: ends every other session.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

PendingFloorEntry.description: Floor entries one source dropped, waiting for a decision (§2.7).

hashes.description: Up to 1,000 of them, 40 hex digits each.

name.description: The file's path, or the list's name.

Preview.description:
What a change would do (§20.10). Counts come from the review queue,
the tombstones, the filter hits of the replay window and the index.

Fields are in the order `POST /filters/preview` has always sent them;
where an assessment is nested in another body, its keys are sorted.

caught_30d.description: Decisions in the replay window by the rules it affects.

core_caught_30d.description: Of those, by the child-safety core.

estimate.description:
Counts from names only (sealed names, no file lists), so files'
evidence isn't re-checked: treat as an estimate.

quarantine.description: Quarantined items it would release now.

removed_from_floor.description: Entries that would leave the locked floor.

stored.description: Stored items whose hide, demote or flag mark it would clear.

tombstones.description: Dropped items it would let be fetched again.

PreviewEstimate.description: A consequence the preview can put a number on, for the UI to format.

name.description:
What it measures: `sockets` (concurrent metadata fetches), `url`
(where the UI will be after a restart), `memory_mib`.

PreviewWarning.description: Something worth knowing before saving; it doesn't stop the save.

example.message: Search stops after the restart, until you turn it back on.

adult_hold.description:
Held only because you relabelled it adult (a correction or a
classification rule) and the Adult-only core caught it: at
`expires_at` it becomes a tombstone rather than being released.

expires_at.description: When its sealed name is deleted and its quarantine ends.

Queue.description:
`GET /filters/queue`: quarantine (never with names) and the replay
window's decisions per rule.

next_cursor.description: The next page of quarantine, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

RebuildEvent.description:
`event: rebuild`: index rebuild progress (§8, the "Index rebuilding"
banner of §10.4), sent when it changes, and once more with `done`.

done.description: Torrents in the new index so far.

unavailable.description: Fields that match nothing until the swap.

RebuildPhase.description: A rebuild's phase; `done` once the new index serves.

ResyncEvent.description:
`event: resync`: events were missed; refetch what the page shows, then
carry on with the events that follow. It has no `id:`.

action.description: Null for an action code this server doesn't know.

shadow_until.description: Shadow mode ends then: until then it only records what it would do.

Sample.description: One example torrent for `POST /filters/test`, never stored or logged.

type.description: A content type (`movie`, `adult`, …), replacing the classifier's.

SampleFile.description: A sample's file: a path, or a path and its size.

SearchHit.description:
One search result: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1), its
relevance and, for a query with a file clause, the files that matched.

composition.description:
What the torrent is made of, by colour group, in the composition
bar's order; groups without files are left out, and it's empty
before classification.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

junk_reasons.description:
Stable reason keys (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1); empty when there are
none or before classification.

matched_files.description:
Positions in the torrent's file list; present only when the query
has a file clause.

resolved_via.description:
How the title was found when the name wasn't informative:
`files`, `folder` or `structure`; null = from the name itself, or
not classified.

title.description: The resolved title; null = not resolved.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

SearchNotice.description: A note on what a search left out.

SearchRequest.description:
`POST /search`'s body, and `GET /search`'s parameters (where `ast` is
refused: send an AST with POST).

oneOf.description:
A query AST, as `/parse` returns it; it must be one the parser
could produce.

cursor.description:
The previous page's `next_cursor`, to read the next page from the
same index snapshot. Send the same `q` (or `ast`), `sort` and
`hidden` with it.

exact.description:
Count every match exactly, even above 100,000 (within a time
budget; `total_approx` says whether it made it). `1` or `true`.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

offset.description: `offset + limit` may not pass 10,000. Not with `cursor`.

q.description: The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both.

sort.description:
`relevance` (the default), or `discovered`, `size` or `files` with
an optional `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending, the default).

canonical.description: The query as the server understood it.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page, read from the same index
snapshot (§8); null on the last page. Opaque, URL-safe, at most
256 characters, valid for 10 minutes after its last use.

notices.description:
What the server left out of these results, for the UI to say:
`adult_hidden` when the query asks for Adult (`type:adult`,
`adult:…`) while "Show adult content" is off, so it matched
nothing adult (§20.9).

stemmed.description:
Few exact matches: plural forms in titles were included too (§8),
ranked after the exact ones.

total.description: Matches in all, not just this page.

total_approx.description:
`total` is an estimate (above 100,000 matches; shown with "≈");
ask with `exact` for the exact count.

restart_required.description:
Fields whose saved value differs from the running one: they take
effect at the next restart.

revision.description:
Goes up by one with every save that changes the section. Send it
back as `if_revision` to refuse a save over someone else's.

SettingField.description: One field of a section, for its form.

env.description: The environment variable that overrides it; null when none does.

help_key.description: Message key of the help text beside the field.

label_key.description: Message key of the field's label.

read_only.description: Never editable in the app (e.g. the data directory).

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

SettingSource.description:
Where a setting's effective value comes from, lowest to highest:
the built-in default, `config.toml`, a change saved in the app, or a
`LODESTAR_*` environment variable.

env.description: The variable that set it when `source` is `env`; null otherwise.

read_only.description:
Can't be changed in the app: set by the environment, or never
editable here.

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

value.description: Any JSON value, of the type the section's schema gives the field.

SettingsBatch.description:
`PATCH /settings` and `POST /settings/preview`: patches for several
sections, `{section: {field: value}}`, each as `PATCH
/settings/{section}` takes it. Saved all together or not at all.

code.description: A stable snake_case identifier to branch on.

message.description: A sentence for people. It never repeats a secret's value.

SettingsErrorEnvelope.description:
A refused settings change: the API's error envelope, plus the
`section` at fault and, for `409 stale_revision`, the current values
of every section that changed meanwhile.

current.description:
On `409 stale_revision`: each stale section's values now, to merge
the edit with.

SettingsEvent.description:
`event: settings`: a section was saved (by any tab, device or API
client) and is now at `revision`. It carries no values: fetch them
with `GET /settings/{section}`.

confirm_adult.description:
The 18+ confirmation, needed when the file turns on an adult
setting (as `PATCH /settings/content` needs it).

revisions.description:
The sections' revisions the dry run reported: the import is refused
with `409 stale_revision` if any changed since.

toml.description: The file's text (TOML), at most 64 KiB.

SettingsPatch.description:
`PATCH /settings/{section}`: some of the section's fields and their
new values, as its schema in `GET /settings` describes. Fields left
out keep their values; an unknown field is refused. `null` resets a
field: its saved value is removed, and the `config.toml` value or the
default applies again.

Two keys aren't fields and are never saved: `if_revision` (the
section's `revision` the edit started from; a save over a newer one is
refused with `409 stale_revision`) and a section's confirmations
(`content`'s `confirm_adult`).

SettingsPreview.description:
`POST /settings/preview`: what a `PATCH /settings` with the same body
would do, without saving it.

SettingsSection.description: One section: its fields and the JSON schema of its values.

schema.description:
A JSON Schema (2020-12) object for the section's values, with
each number field's bounds as `minimum`/`maximum`.

allOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

oneOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

SettingsTest.description: `POST /settings/test`: what to test, with the values on screen.

message.description: A sentence for people; never the URL or a credential.

example.message: The client refused the user name or password.

SettingsTestResult.description:
`POST /settings/test`: the result, shown beside the button. Nothing is
saved either way.

api_version.description: The client's API version, when it has one apart from its version.

oneOf.description: Why it failed; null when `ok`.

version.description: The client's version, as it reports it; null unless `ok`.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /setup`: claims the instance.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

token.description:
The one-time token printed to the logs (`XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, any
case).

Strictness.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: what the lists would block, and a warning
matched to it (§2.9, §20.13).

estimate.description:
Some figures are the catalog's measurements of lists not fetched
yet, and lists may overlap: a lower bound.

floor_hashes.description: Torrents a floor-marked list blocks by hash.

ipv4_public_share.description: The share of public IPv4 blocked (0–1); the level reads this.

ipv4_share.description: The share of all IPv4 blocked (0–1).

ipv6_share.description: The share of IPv6 global unicast blocked (0–1).

unknown.description: Lists never fetched, so what they block isn't known.

StrictnessBody.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: a candidate set of lists to assess,
subscriptions by id and catalog lists by key (`lodestar lists`), in
any mix.

StrictnessList.description: One list's figures in a [`Strictness`]; null where unknown.

measured.description: The figures are a catalog measurement, not this list's data.

SwarmSample.description:
One day or week of swarm history. Counts saturate at 65,534; null is
a gap.

at.description:
The start of the UTC day, or of the week (epoch day / 7: weeks
start on Thursday).

TestBody.description: `POST /filters/test`: a draft rule and examples to try it on.

oneOf.description: What the current rules decide; null = nothing.

draft.description: Whether the draft matches; null without a draft.

shadow.description: Rules in shadow mode that would have decided.

adult_hold.description: Left by an adult hold's quarantine at the 30-day purge.

Tombstones.description:
`GET /filters/tombstones`: dropped torrents, by hash and rule (no
names), so one can be found and released.

next_cursor.description: The next page, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

Topic.description: What a client subscribes to with `?topics=`.

TorrentDetail.description:
`GET /torrents/{hash}`: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1),
its swarm section (§7.2) and the first 500 files.

The swarm fields are `null` until swarm health is served (M4): null is
"never scraped", never 0.

dht_peers.description: BEP 33 estimate of peers (always approximate); null = no estimate.

dht_seeds.description: BEP 33 estimate of seeds (always approximate); null = no estimate.

file_list.description: The first files, in the torrent's order; the rest via `/files`.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

oneOf.description:
14 daily and 26 weekly samples, newest first; null = no history
kept.

swarm_trend.description:
Seeders per day over the last week; null = fewer than 3 daily
samples.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

TorrentsEvent.description:
`event: torrents`: torrents became searchable. Commits close together
may arrive as one event.

added.description:
Torrents new to the index since the previous `torrents` event;
can be 0 when only `max_id` moved on.

max_id.description: The highest torrent id searchable now.

Error.description: Any failure: the error envelope. `error.code` is stable; branch on it.

session.name: lodestar_session
session.description: The session cookie `/setup`, `/login` and `/password` set. HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict.
